rule.description: Persistence: registry Run key value added

_note: Real, live-fired alert for Rules/persistence-run-key-cron.xml's Windows rule (100211), run against dc01-lab via `reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" /v WazuhLabTest /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Windows\Temp\update.exe" /f`. This closes out the investigation documented in Rules/persistence-run-key-cron.xml and Evidence/t1053-windows-validation.json: the if_sid=92302 chaining fix (merged in #59) never actually reached the manager on the first deployment attempt - the container's /var/ossec/etc/rules/persistence-run-key-cron.xml was still the pre-chaining revision (confirmed via a `docker exec ... cat` of the on-disk file, which showed the older if_group=sysmon_event_13 version despite the merged fix), so every post-merge live test kept resolving to the community rule 92302, not 100211. A fresh `docker cp` of the actual merged file, verified on-disk before restarting, resolved it: rule 100211 fired at level 12 (firedtimes: 1) and correctly superseded both 92302 (image=reg.exe match) and 92041 (Base64-like pattern heuristic) on the same underlying Sysmon Event ID 13. Captured verbatim via `docker exec single-node-wazuh.manager-1 sh -c 'grep -F "WazuhLabTest" /var/ossec/logs/alerts/alerts.json'`, no content altered. This is the last of the 6 combos (3 MITRE techniques x 2 platforms) to get a genuine live-fired alert.
